html:
The Kalmar Union joined the kingdoms of Denmark, Sweden and Norway under a single monarch from 1397 to 1523. On the Americas map it appears in 1400 and 1500 because it included Norway's Atlantic lands: Iceland, the Faroes and Greenland.

It was the work of Margaret I, who ruled Denmark and Norway and won Sweden. In 1397 her young great nephew, Eric of Pomerania, was crowned king of all three at Kalmar in Sweden. One aim was to balance the power of the German merchants of the Hanseatic League in the Baltic.

The union was always shaky. Sweden's nobles resented Danish rule and Danish taxes, and Sweden often had its own regent. In 1520 the Danish king Christian II took Stockholm and had scores of Swedish nobles executed, the Stockholm Bloodbath. The revolt that followed made Gustav Vasa king of Sweden in 1523. Denmark and Norway stayed together as Denmark Norway until 1814.

Far away, the Norse settlements in Greenland faded during the union years; the last written record is of a wedding in 1408.
